problems.title: Clear fractional coefficients
problems.question: Solve $2-\frac{3x-7}{4}+\frac{x+17}{5}=0$.
formulas: The common denominator of 4 and 5 is 20.
steps: The equation becomes 40-5(3x-7)+4(x+17)=0.
Expanding gives 143-11x=0.
Therefore x=13; substitution makes both fractional terms cancel the constant.

problems.title: Eliminate a variable in a fractional system
problems.question: Solve $\frac{x+1}{3}-\frac{y+2}{4}=\frac{2(x-y)}5$, $\frac{x-3}{4}-\frac{y-3}{3}=2y-x$.
problems.idea: Clear denominators separately, then eliminate y.
formulas: Multiplying by a common denominator produces an equivalent equation.
steps: Multiply the first equation by 60: 20(x+1)-15(y+2)=24(x-y), giving -4x+9y=10.
Multiply the second by 12: 3(x-3)-4(y-3)=24y-12x, giving 15x-28y=-3.
Multiply the first simplified equation by 28 and the second by 9, then add: 23x=253, so x=11.
Substitute: -44+9y=10, so y=6.

problems.title: Intersecting chords and four arcs
problems.question: The endpoints of two intersecting chords divide a circle into consecutive arcs in ratio 1:4:3:10. Find the acute angle between the chords.
problems.idea: Opposite arcs are paired in the chord-angle formula.
formulas: Intersecting-chord angle=half the sum of its opposite intercepted arcs.
steps: The ratio sum is 18, so each unit is 20°. The arcs are 20°,80°,60°,200°.
One pair of opposite arcs sums to 20°+60°=80°, giving angle 40°.
The other pair gives (80°+200°)/2=140°.

problems.title: Recover a missing equation and compare coefficients
problems.question: For which a does $-3x-y=a+5$, $(a-3)x-2y=4$ have infinitely many solutions?
problems.idea: Both equations must represent the same line.
formulas: Two nontrivial linear equations have infinitely many common solutions exactly when their coefficients and constants are proportional.
steps: The second y-coefficient is twice the first, so the entire second equation must be twice the first.
Compare x-coefficients: a-3=2·(-3)=-6, giving a=-3.
Compare constants at that value: 2(a+5)=2·2=4, as required.
The second equation then is -6x-2y=4, exactly twice -3x-y=2.
problems.note: The second equation is missing from the converted PDF. It was recovered from the original Word document’s embedded equation: (a-3)x-2y=4.

problems.title: Reverse the digits of a two-digit number
problems.question: Adding 63 to a two-digit number reverses its digits. Find every such number.
problems.idea: Represent the tens and units digits separately.
formulas: A two-digit number with digits t,u equals 10t+u.
steps: The condition is 10t+u+63=10u+t, so 9(u-t)=63 and u=t+7.
Since t≥1 and u≤9, t can be 1 or 2.
The corresponding numbers are 18 and 29; indeed 18+63=81 and 29+63=92.

problems.title: Substitute to obtain a quadratic system
problems.question: Solve $4x^2+1=y^2+4x$, $y-x=3$.
problems.idea: Use the linear equation to replace y.
formulas: If y=x+3, substitute that expression into the other equation.
steps: The first equation becomes 4x²+1=(x+3)²+4x.
Simplify to 3x²-10x-8=0=(3x+2)(x-4).
Thus x=4 or x=-2/3. Adding 3 gives y=7 or y=7/3.

problems.title: A circle centred at a right-angle vertex
problems.question: ABC is right-angled at C. The circle centred at C with radius AC meets hypotenuse AB again at D and leg CB at E. Given B=37°, find the minor arcs AD and DE.
problems.idea: Use isosceles triangle ACD to find its central angle.
formulas: Equal radii give CA=CD; a minor arc has the measure of its central angle.
steps: In ACD, angles CAD and ADC are 53°, so ACD=180°-106°=74°.
Thus minor arc AD=74°. The right angle ACE=90° leaves DCE=90°-74°=16°.

problems.title: Positive integer coordinates on a line
problems.question: Find all points with positive integer coordinates on the line through A(0,12) and B(15,0).
problems.idea: Write the intercept equation with integer coefficients.
steps: Reducing modulo 5 shows 4x is divisible by 5, so x=5k.
Substitution gives y=12-4k.
Positivity requires k≥1 and 12-4k≥1, so k=1 or 2.
problems.note: Natural coordinates are taken as positive. If zero is included in that convention, also include the endpoints (0,12) and (15,0).

problems.title: Compare shares of the same royalty total
problems.question: Royalties are split 8:6:5. With a split of 7:5:4, one author would receive 25 lari more. Find the total.
problems.idea: Compare each author’s fraction, using the correct total parts.
formulas: A share with ratio part k and total ratio sum S is k/S of the total.
steps: The first author’s share rises from 8/19 to 7/16; the difference is (133-128)/304=5/304.
The second share falls from 6/19 to 5/16, and the third falls from 5/19 to 4/16. Thus only the first author gains.
If T is the total, (5/304)T=25, giving T=25·304/5=1520.

problems.title: An excircle distance from the opposite vertex
problems.question: The A-excircle touches BC and the extensions of AB and AC. B=10°, C=50°, and the triangle perimeter is 17.6 cm. Find AO, where O is the excentre.
problems.idea: Combine the tangent length from A with a 30° right triangle.
formulas: Tangent lengths from A to the A-excircle equal the semiperimeter s; the excentre lies on the internal bisector of A.
steps: A=180°-10°-50°=120°, so the angle between AO and a side is 60°.
The tangent distance AT from A to a contact point on a side extension equals s=17.6/2=8.8.
Radius OT is perpendicular to AT, so cos60°=AT/AO=1/2.
Thus AO=2AT=17.6.
